t: None of the funds provided or otherwise made available in this Act shall be available to carry out section 872 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 452).

fable.w: This is an appropriations limitation that bars the use of funds to carry out a reorganization authority under the Homeland Security Act. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. It only restricts federal spending.
fable.s: None of the funds provided or otherwise made available in this Act shall be available to carry out section 872 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 452).

qwen_block.w: This section is a funding restriction (a 'notwithstanding' or 'none of the funds' provision) that prohibits the use of appropriated money for a specific statutory section. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) before a federal decision is made. It is purely a budgetary constraint.
qwen_block.s: None of the funds provided or otherwise made available in this Act shall be available to carry out section 872 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 452).

opus.w: This section only limits the use of funds. It bars spending to carry out the Department of Homeland Security's internal reorganization authority. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public takes part in any federal decision. The referenced provision involves at most notice to Congress, which is inside the federal government, so there is no participation.
opus.s: None of the funds provided or otherwise made available in this Act shall be available to carry out section 872 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 452).
opus.b: I'd label this **No**. The section only limits funding. It says no money in the Act may be used for section 872 of the Homeland Security Act, which is the Secretary's power to reorganize the Department internally. One could read "carry out section 872" as hiding some outside process. But section 872 only calls for notice to Congress, which is inside the federal government. No one outside the government is consulted, asked for comment, given a hearing, or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a funding restriction that prohibits the use of appropriated funds to carry out a specific provision of another act. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, advisory committees, consultation with outside entities, or other forms of participation as defined. It merely limits the executive branch's ability to spend money on a specific activity.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds provided or otherwise made available in this Act shall be available to carry out section 872 of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 452).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section references "section 872 of the Homeland Security Act," and that section might involve participation, this section implicitly involves participation. However, this section is merely a funding restriction (a "riders" or "anomaly" provision) that prohibits the use of funds for a specific statutory provision. It does not itself create, require, or describe any process of consultation, coordination, or public input. It simply blocks funding.
